briefing.summary: Markets are staging a powerful broad-based rally entering Friday, with the S&P now 9 consecutive sessions higher (+5.38% over 20 days) and the regime firmly Risk-On at 71% confidence. Semis are the clear leadership engine (SMH +3.17%), cyclicals are broadly outperforming defensives, and international markets are confirming the move — yet the rally is running into overbought territory near a 52-week low base with VIX still elevated at 22.68 and Fear & Greed at extreme fear (0), creating a paradoxical setup where sentiment hasn't caught up to price. The story here is a technical squeeze and cyclical rotation rather than a clean fundamental re-rating — trade it with eyes open.

sections.title: 🧭 Overall Market Posture & Regime
sections.content: SIGNAL classifies today as RISK-ON with 71% confidence and a directional bias of +41. Futures are pointing +1.49% pre-market, the Russell 2000 is leading large-caps by 0.78 percentage points — a classic risk-on signal — and international markets are broadly green with DAX +2.62% and Hang Seng +1.74% providing global confirmation. However, two flags demand respect: (1) The S&P is pressing near a 52-week LOW, not a high — this is a relief rally from oversold conditions, not momentum off a breakout. (2) Fear & Greed sits at 0 (extreme fear) while price action is bullish — this divergence suggests the rally is being driven by short covering and positioning unwinds rather than genuine conviction buying. The 9-day win streak is statistically overbought, and any fade Friday afternoon would be technically normal. Conviction penalty on shorts is -8 today, so the regime says: don't fight the tape, but size longs with awareness of the stretched run.

sections.title: 🔄 Sector Rotation & Relative Strength
sections.content: Every sector closed green — a rare broad-tape day — but the internal rankings tell the real story. The leadership stack is: Semis (SMH +3.17%) → Financials (XLF +2.07%) → Industrials (XLI +1.79%) → Materials (XLB +1.69%) → Tech (XLK +1.67%). This is a textbook cyclical rotation sequence. Semis leading by a wide margin signals AI/tech infrastructure demand is re-pricing; their outperformance of 1.5pp over the next best sector is significant. Financials at #2 suggest the yield curve steepening (2-10 at +31bps) is being read as margin-positive for banks. The defensive tail — Utilities (+0.78%) and Staples (+0.54%) — lagging the tape by 100-170bps confirms money is moving toward risk. Korea leading internationally (embedded in the regime factors) reinforces semiconductor fab demand as a real-economy signal, not just a narrative. OVERWEIGHT: Semis, Tech, Financials, Materials (China recovery play). UNDERWEIGHT: Utilities, Staples.

sections.title: 📈 Yield Curve & Rate Signals
sections.content: The 10-year Treasury yield is at 4.32%, up +2.15% on the session — rates rising alongside equities is a risk-on confirmation (growth expectations driving the move, not inflation fear). The 2-10 spread has steepened to +31bps and the 3M-10Y spread is barely positive at +11bps — the curve is no longer inverted but remains historically flat, suggesting the market is pricing a soft-landing path rather than imminent recession. The modest steepening is constructive for Financials (XLF) and rate-sensitive cyclicals. Watch the 4.40% level on the 10Y — a break above that on strong jobs data today (NFP Friday) could pressure rate-sensitive growth stocks like high-multiple tech and REITs (XLRE only +1.23%, already the relative laggard in the cyclical complex). The VIX term structure in contango signals traders expect volatility to remain elevated but are not pricing a near-term spike — consistent with a market that's healing but not yet comfortable.

sections.title: 💱 Currency & Commodity Flows
sections.content: USD/JPY +1.71% to 145.45 is a significant risk-on signal — yen weakness reflects unwinding of safe-haven positioning and carry trade reactivation. The dollar index at 100.0 (-0.25%) is softening against the broader basket despite the yen move, which is EUR/USD constructive (1.13) and consistent with global reflation trade. The soft dollar is a tailwind for Materials (XLB) and Emerging Markets. Copper +1.0% is the macro confirmation signal here — Dr. Copper doesn't lie, and its strength alongside Materials outperformance suggests the China recovery trade has legs. However, WTI crude at $58.29 (-1.6%) is a notable divergence — oil falling while copper and risk assets rally suggests this isn't a pure demand-driven commodity move; rather, OPEC supply dynamics or demand skepticism on energy specifically. Gold at $3,231.90 (+0.68%) is holding gains despite risk-on conditions, suggesting investors haven't fully abandoned hedges — smart money is running with one hand on the parachute. Bitcoin -1.05% is a mild red flag: crypto typically leads risk-on extensions, and its underperformance vs equities today could signal the rally's risk appetite has limits.

sections.title: ⚠️ Risk Factors & Contrarian Signals
sections.content: Five risks to monitor entering Friday's session: (1) OVERBOUGHT STRETCH — 9 consecutive up days is a 2-sigma event. Mean reversion risk is real, particularly into the weekly close when Friday afternoon profit-taking is common. (2) F&G AT ZERO vs. PRICE ACTION — Extreme fear while prices rally is a short-squeeze dynamic. When the squeeze exhausts, there's no natural buyer waiting. (3) VIX AT 22.68 — Still 'elevated' despite the -7.8% drop. Options markets are not fully capitulating on fear. A vol event (geopolitical, data shock) could re-spike quickly. (4) CRYPTO LAGGING — Bitcoin -1.05% and Ethereum -0.48% on a strong equity day. In genuine risk-on regimes, crypto participates or leads. Divergence here is a yellow flag. (5) NFP RELEASE (today) — It's Jobs Friday. A strong print could push 10Y above 4.40% and trigger a 'good news is bad news' rate shock. A weak print validates slowdown fears and tests whether this rally has fundamental legs. Zero breadth above 200 DMA remains the structural concern — this is a price recovery, not a breadth thrust.

scenarios.event: NFP Jobs Report — Strong Print (>200K, beats consensus)

scenarios.condition: If payrolls beat significantly AND wages remain contained (<0.3% MoM)
scenarios.implication: Goldilocks read — growth without inflation pressure. 10Y holds below 4.40%, equities extend, dollar stays soft. Risk-on confirmation. Semis, Financials, Industrials add to gains. The 9-day streak becomes 10.
scenarios.trade: Add to SMH, XLF on the open dip; trim into 3:30pm if SPY approaches the 20-day resistance level. Target SMH continuation toward the $220 zone.

scenarios.condition: If payrolls beat AND wages surprise hot (>0.4% MoM)
scenarios.implication: Stagflation-adjacent read — good jobs but inflationary. 10Y spikes toward 4.50%+, rate-sensitive growth sells off hard (XLK, XLRE), dollar rips. The risk-on rally stalls or reverses. Defensives and energy could catch a bid on the re-pricing.
scenarios.trade: Reduce tech/semi longs preemptively if wage data hot; consider TBT (short bonds) or XLF as a rate-beneficiary hedge. Avoid adding XLRE or XLU.

scenarios.event: Semis Continue to Lead — AI/Tech Rotation Continuation

scenarios.condition: If SMH holds above its prior session close and breaks technical resistance intraday
scenarios.implication: The AI infrastructure thesis is being re-priced after recent de-rating. Korea leading (fab demand signal) + copper strength + SMH momentum = rare alignment. A breakout here pulls XLK and QQQ with it and could trigger systematic buying from momentum algos.
scenarios.trade: Long SMH with a tight stop below the morning low; target a 2-3% extension. Secondary play: NVDA, AVGO as component leaders. Conviction: HIGH (regime overweight semis, multiple confirming signals).

scenarios.condition: If SMH fades after an opening gap-up
scenarios.implication: Gap-fill risk after +3.17% session and 9 consecutive up days. A fade would signal the short-squeeze dynamics are exhausting. Watch for volume confirmation — low-volume gap-up fades are more dangerous than high-volume ones.
scenarios.trade: If SMH gaps up >1% and fades within first 30 minutes on declining volume, reduce position or tighten stops. Do NOT short into the regime — take the penalty (-8 conviction) off the table.

scenarios.condition: If USD/JPY reverses sharply below 144.00 during Friday's session (BOJ commentary, risk-off catalyst)
scenarios.implication: Yen strength = carry trade unwinding = forced deleveraging across risk assets. This is the single fastest transmission mechanism from currency to equity shock. VIX would re-spike from 22.68, gold would accelerate, equities would give back a significant portion of the 9-day rally. The extreme fear F&G reading (0) would prove prescient.
scenarios.trade: This is the tail-risk scenario. If USD/JPY cracks 144 intraday, reduce all cyclical longs immediately, rotate defensive (XLU, XLP, GLD). The carry unwind is non-linear — it moves faster than stops can protect. Monitor USD/JPY in real-time as your risk dashboard canary.

scenarios.condition: If USD/JPY holds above 145 and continues toward 146+
scenarios.implication: Carry trade fully back on. Japanese equities (Nikkei already +1.04%) continue to run, global reflation trade extends, risk appetite confirmed. Materials, EM, and cyclicals get additional tailwind from the dollar softness against non-JPY currencies.
scenarios.trade: Hold or add Materials (XLB) and consider an EWJ (Japan ETF) position as a direct Nikkei/yen-carry beneficiary. The China recovery trade in Materials is additive here — copper + yen carry + DAX strength = coordinated global risk-on.

opusReviewNotes:
The most glaring problem with this algorithm is its extreme passivity: 151 no-trade days out of 180 trials (83.9%). The algorithm is leaving enormous amounts of alpha on the table. When it does trade, it wins only 31% of the time, but its profit factor of 19.81 suggests winners are massive relative to losers — this is a classic trend-following profile being applied to day trading, which creates a fundamental mismatch. The algorithm needs to trade more frequently with tighter conviction thresholds, not less.

Looking at the last 10 trials, the pipeline's most critical failure is the disconnect between regime identification and trade generation. Trial 173 identified a CRISIS regime at 90% confidence on April 9, 2025 — the day after a historic +9.5% S&P surge likely driven by a tariff pause — yet generated zero trades. This was arguably one of the highest-conviction trading days in the entire dataset. A crisis regime with a massive relief rally screams for momentum-continuation longs in high-beta names (QQQ, TQQQ, ARKK, SMH) or mean-reversion shorts if you believed the rally was a dead-cat bounce. Similarly, Trial 180 had a risk-on regime at 71% confidence with a 9-session winning streak and generated nothing. Trial 175 identified risk-off at 60% confidence near 52-week lows and did nothing. The regime classifier is working reasonably well — the trade generator is broken.

Trial 177 is the lone success in the last 10: rotation regime on Oct 2, 2024, with defense stocks RTX (+1.14%) and LMT (+0.85%) both winning. This reveals what works — sector rotation plays where the catalyst is clear (geopolitical tensions driving defense), technicals align (sector leadership), and the trade is WITH the rotation, not against it. The algorithm should be pattern-matching more aggressively to this template: identify WHERE capital is flowing and ride it, rather than trying to pick bottoms or tops.

Dimension predictive power is remarkably flat (71.5-74.6 range across all 7 dimensions), which suggests either the scoring rubric lacks discriminatory power or the sample size (13) is too small to differentiate. However, timingUrgency (74.6) and catalystClarity (74.5) show marginal edges over volumeLiquidity (71.5) and marketAlignment (71.6). The weight evolution shows catalystClarity has consistently been the highest-weighted dimension (12.6%-24.9%), which aligns with its predictive power. But marketAlignment has been volatile (7.4%-19.8%), suggesting the algorithm can't decide if macro alignment matters — it does, but only as a veto/confirmation, not a primary signal.

The 3 stop-loss hits averaging -6.3% are devastating for a day-trading algorithm. A 6.3% intraday loss should never happen with proper position sizing and stop discipline. The worst trials (75, 30, 55) all show trades that went against prevailing conditions: BRK.B short during what was likely a bullish market, SNOW long during a period of growth-stock weakness, and three simultaneous energy/materials longs (VLO, CMC, AYI) that suggest over-concentration in a single theme. The algorithm needs hard caps: max 1-2% stop loss per trade, max 1 trade per sector, and position sizing inversely proportional to volatility.
